---
title: "Figure 4 (tentative B) — the interval axis on its own axis: where the interval-aware and interval-naive members meet, and where they part"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document

<!--
TENTATIVE. Written 2026-08-04. Not numbered, not in the manuscript. Companion to
figure_4_rays.Rmd, which holds two design variables fixed and moves the third out of one corner.
This one does the opposite: it puts the acquisition interval on the x axis, which no figure in the
set currently does, and runs it at BOTH ends of the channel axis.

WHY BOTH ENDS. The rays notebook launches its interval ray from N_ch = 10, which is the right place
to verify that a pair CLOSES and the wrong place to show that it OPENS. Measured in Figure 4-figure
supplement 4, the R-to-IR gap on the k_off correlation is about 0.11 at N_ch = 10 and about 0.55 at
N_ch = 10^4, a factor five. A single ray from the few-channel corner therefore understates the
interval effect by construction. Two columns, one per end, cost nothing and measure the interaction
that a one-at-a-time design cannot see.

WHAT IS ON THE PAGE
  x        Delta*k_off, the acquisition interval in units of the closing time constant, log, the
           seven values swept inside every cell: 0.01 0.02 0.05 0.1 0.2 0.5 1
  rows     the three quantities: bias, then the two components of the distortion
  columns  the two ends of the channel axis
  colour   the pair
  linetype interval-naive (dashed) against interval-aware (solid)
  band     the bootstrap 95 per cent over resampled GROUPS, drawn as an explicit bar because a
           ribbon that narrow is invisible; see the bootstrap note below for what it does and does
           not mean

THE READING, in one sentence each.
  LEFT EDGE. The two members of a pair must lie on top of each other, because at Delta*k_off = 0.01
  the interval average and the instantaneous sample differ by about 2 per cent. That is a limit the
  implementation must satisfy and it does not come from the code under test.
  RIGHT EDGE. They must part, and the size of the parting IS the interval axis, measured.
  ACROSS COLUMNS. If the parting is larger at N_ch = 10^4 than at N_ch = 10, the two design axes
  interact, which is worth stating because every other figure in the set marginalises one of them.

TRAP, inherited from supplement 4 and the reason the interval was kept inside a band there: the
delta dependence is NOT monotone, and the point Delta*k_off = 1 sits at a kappa ~ 1e5 corner where
the sample distortion deflates to about 0.44. Expect the last point of every curve to misbehave. It
is a property of that cell, not of the members, and the caption must say so rather than smooth it.

ANCHORS. bias is battery_sim_G at theta_sim; sample and correlation are battery_pool_G at
theta_pool. At theta_pool the score vanishes by construction, so a bias read there is zero by
definition and means nothing. The row strip carries the anchor so the three rows are never read as
three views of one computation.

NOISE is held at the label 0.1 throughout, which is the lowest level at which every member exists.
IR alone reaches 0.05.

THE BOOTSTRAP, verified against the code, because what it resamples decides what the bar means.

  IT IS THE CLASSICAL NONPARAMETRIC BOOTSTRAP, not the Poisson one. generate_bootstrap_indices
  (legacy/bootstrap.h:44) draws n indices uniformly with replacement at fixed resample size, and
  bootstrap_it pre-draws every replicate's indices serially so the result is seed-reproducible
  independently of the thread count. There is a Moment_poisson_bootstrap class in the tree; it is
  never instantiated anywhere and is dead code. Do not describe this as a Poisson bootstrap.

  IT RESAMPLES GROUPS, NOT RECORDINGS. src/core/likelihood.cpp:4278 says so in capitals, and :4622
  gives the reason: the per-group theta-hat are the iid units, and each resampled group is expanded
  to its recordings inside the computation. With group_size 100 over 10^4 recordings that is about a
  hundred units, and the same comment warns that few groups collapse the intervals. The width of the
  bar therefore depends in part on how the ensemble was grouped, which is a design decision and not
  a property of the estimator. B = 100 replicates, readable from the bootstrap_count column.

  THE CENTRE IS THE MEDIAN, quantile_level 0.5, and not the emitted mean. Every quantity here is a
  nonlinear functional of accumulated moments, a ratio of matrices or a product of eigenvalues, so
  the mean over replicates is not the statistic of the full ensemble: there is a Jensen bias, and
  this project has already measured one instance (the affine-invariant distance emitted as
  E_boot[d_AI] is biased up near the identity). For a positive right-skewed bootstrap distribution
  the mean sits above the median, which pushes a distortion away from 1 and would manufacture
  exactly the gap this figure exists to test.

  DO NOT TRANSFER THIS READING to the time-resolved diagnostics. Those go through
  bootstrap_it_two_to_Probit with two INDEPENDENT index sets and no pairing, and the header of
  bootstrap_it_two states that there the bootstrap is a comparison-of-estimators tool and not a
  re-recording-variance estimator. Different family, different meaning.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r constants}
DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
NOISE     <- "0.1"
NCH_ENDS  <- c(10, 10000)

PAIRS <- tribble(
  ~pair,      ~naive,       ~aware,
  "LSE/ILSE", "macro_LSE",  "macro_ILSE",
  "NR/INR",   "macro_NR",   "macro_INR",
  "R/IR",     "macro_R",    "macro_IR"
)
PAIR_COL <- c("LSE/ILSE" = "#999999", "NR/INR" = "#D55E00", "R/IR" = "#0072B2")

# NOTE: strip labels are parsed as plotmath (label_parsed), so a literal space is a syntax error.
# Spaces are written as ~ and every label must stay a valid R expression.
QTY <- tribble(
  ~qty,     ~component,                                            ~battery,          ~lab,                         ~diag,
  "bias",   "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Distortion_Induced_Bias",  "battery_sim_G",   "bias~at~theta[sim]",         FALSE,
  "sample", "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Sample_Distortion",        "battery_pool_G",  "sample~at~theta[pool]",      TRUE,
  "corr",   "Probit_statistics_Likelihood_Correlation_Distortion", "battery_pool_G",  "correlation~at~theta[pool]", TRUE
)
# diag: the two distortions are MATRICES and the figure wants their diagonal, so param_index must
# equal param_col. The bias is a VECTOR: its param_col is empty, the equality evaluates to NA, and
# filtering on it silently drops every bias row.

PARAMS  <- c(off = 1, Num_ch_mean = 5)
PAR_LAB <- c(off = "k[off]", Num_ch_mean = "N[ch]")

findf <- function(nch, algo, z, kind) {
  f <- file.path(DATA_DIRS,
       sprintf("figure_3_G_nch_%d_nsim_10000_%s_noise_%s_%s.csv", nch, algo, z, kind))
  f <- f[file.exists(f)]
  if (!length(f)) NA_character_ else f[1]
}
```

```{r data}
grid <- expand_grid(PAIRS, nch = NCH_ENDS) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(naive, aware), names_to = "member", values_to = "algo") %>%
  mutate(member = if_else(member == "naive", "interval-naive", "interval-aware"))

d <- pmap_dfr(QTY, function(qty, component, battery, lab, diag) {
  pmap_dfr(grid, function(pair, nch, member, algo) {
    f <- findf(nch, algo, NOISE, battery)
    if (is.na(f)) return(NULL)
    read.csv(f, skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      filter(component_path == component,
             if (diag) param_index == param_col else TRUE, param_index %in% PARAMS,
             statistic == "value",
             probit == "quantile", quantile_level %in% c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)) %>%
      transmute(pair, nch, member, qty,
                interval = as.numeric(interval_in_tau),
                param = names(PARAMS)[match(param_index, PARAMS)],
                key = case_when(quantile_level == 0.5   ~ "mid",
                              quantile_level == 0.025 ~ "lo",
                              TRUE                    ~ "hi"),
                value)
  })
})
stopifnot(nrow(d) > 0)

# keep only pairs where BOTH members are present at BOTH ends, so no column is half a comparison
ok <- d %>% distinct(pair, nch, member) %>% count(pair, nch) %>%
      group_by(pair) %>% filter(all(n == 2), n_distinct(nch) == length(NCH_ENDS)) %>%
      ungroup() %>% distinct(pair) %>% pull(pair)
cat("pairs complete at both ends:", paste(ok, collapse = " "), "\n")

dw <- d %>% filter(pair %in% ok) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = key, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(qty  = factor(qty, levels = QTY$qty, labels = QTY$lab),
         nlab = factor(sprintf("N[ch] == %d", nch), levels = sprintf("N[ch] == %d", NCH_ENDS)),
         member = factor(member, levels = c("interval-naive", "interval-aware")))
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 6.0, fig.height = 6.4}
# ONE PAIR PER COLUMN, AND EACH PAIR ON ITS OWN Y SCALE, composed with patchwork rather than
# facetted: facet_grid shares its free scales along a row, so pairs in the columns of one grid land
# on a common axis and the smaller one collapses.
#
# NO DASHED LINES. Both members are solid and separated by colour. The two channel counts are the
# row instead, since a fourth series in a panel would need a fourth colour and the comparison the
# figure exists for is the one between the two members.
#
# SCALES follow figure_6B.Rmd: raw values in the data, the transform done by the scale. BIAS IS A
# SEPARATE FIGURE because it is null at 0 and signed and cannot share a log axis with a ratio.
suppressMessages(library(patchwork))
X_BRK    <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1)
MEM_COL  <- c("interval-naive" = "#D55E00", "interval-aware" = "#0072B2")
DIST_BRK <- c(0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.3, 1.6, 2, 3, 5)
base_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(.14, "cm"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 6.5),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5.5),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.size = unit(.6, "lines"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5), plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = .5),
        plot.margin = margin(3, 4, 2, 3))

one_pair <- function(dd, pr, logy, ylab, fac) {
  g <- ggplot(filter(dd, pair == pr), aes(interval, mid, colour = member, fill = member)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = if (logy) 1 else 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = .45, alpha = .8) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .5) + geom_point(size = .9) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = X_BRK, labels = as.character(X_BRK)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = MEM_COL) + scale_fill_manual(values = MEM_COL) +
    labs(x = expression(widetilde(Delta) == Delta %.% k[off]), y = ylab, colour = NULL, fill = NULL, title = pr) +
    fac + base_theme
  if (logy) g <- g + scale_y_log10(breaks = DIST_BRK, labels = as.character(DIST_BRK))
  g
}

for (pp in names(PARAMS)) {
  for (blk in list(list(sel = QTY$lab[-1], logy = TRUE, tag = "distortion", h = 6.0,
                        ylab = "distortion (null = 1)",
                        fac = facet_grid(nlab + qty ~ ., scales = "free_y",
                                         labeller = label_parsed)),
                   list(sel = QTY$lab[1], logy = FALSE, tag = "bias", h = 4.0,
                        ylab = expression("bias  ("*log[10]~units*")"),
                        fac = facet_grid(nlab ~ ., scales = "free_y",
                                         labeller = label_parsed)))) {
    dd <- dw %>% filter(param == pp, qty %in% blk$sel)
    prs <- unique(as.character(dd$pair))
    if (!length(prs)) next
    gl <- lapply(prs, function(pr)
      one_pair(dd, pr, blk$logy, if (pr == prs[1]) blk$ylab else NULL, blk$fac))
    g <- wrap_plots(gl, nrow = 1) +
      plot_annotation(subtitle = parse(text = PAR_LAB[pp])) +
      plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    print(g)
    ggsave(sprintf("Figure_4_interval_pairs_%s_%s.pdf", blk$tag, pp), g,
           width = 3.0 * length(prs), height = blk$h)
  }
}
```

```{r closure-and-opening}
# The two numbers this figure exists to produce.
gap <- dw %>%
  select(pair, nch, qty, param, member, interval, mid) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = member, values_from = mid) %>%
  mutate(rel_gap = abs(`interval-aware` - `interval-naive`) /
                   pmax(abs(`interval-naive`), 1e-12))

cat("\n=== CLOSURE at the short end (Delta*k_off = 0.01): should be a few per cent ===\n")
gap %>% filter(interval == 0.01) %>% arrange(desc(rel_gap)) %>% print(n = 40)

cat("\n=== OPENING: relative gap at the long end over the short end ===\n")
gap %>% filter(interval %in% c(0.01, 1)) %>%
  select(pair, nch, qty, param, interval, rel_gap) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = interval, values_from = rel_gap, names_prefix = "d") %>%
  mutate(fold = d1 / pmax(d0.01, 1e-12)) %>% arrange(desc(fold)) %>% print(n = 40)
```
